## Description

> Write. Nothing else. A calm writing app. Your notes stay plain files in your own GitHub.
>
> Find anything. Instantly. Notes, commands and settings, one keystroke away.
>
> Make it yours. Ten built-in themes, light and dark.
>
> Your notes, in folders. Plain Markdown files you can see, move and keep.
>
> Every note is a Markdown file in a folder you choose. Sign in with your own GitHub account and Focus Notes backs your notes up to your own repository, or keep them on this computer only.
>
> Free and open source, under the MIT License.
>
> The app talks only to your computer and to GitHub, with your own account, to save and back up your notes. There's no Focus Notes server and no Focus Notes account.
>
> Start writing.

## Product features

- Spotlight: Find anything. Instantly. Notes, commands and settings, one keystroke away.
- Themes: Make it yours. Ten built-in themes, light and dark.
- Files: Your notes, in folders. Plain Markdown files you can see, move and keep.
- Works offline: notes are plain files on your computer, backed up to your own GitHub repository when you're online.
- Private notes stay in your own private repository; share a sealed copy with only the people you choose.
- A command-line tool and an MCP server, so the agents you allow can read and write notes, each change kept and undoable.

## Notes for certification

> No account is needed to test the app: on the first screen choose "Just use this computer for now" and start writing; notes are saved as Markdown files in Documents\Focus Notes. Signing in to GitHub is optional and only backs notes up to the tester's own repository. Closing the window keeps Focus Notes running in the notification area, so it opens again at once; right-click its icon there and choose "Quit Focus Notes" to quit. The app declares runFullTrust because it's a desktop (Electron) app, the focus-notes: link scheme to open a note from a link, and the focus-notes command-line alias. Focus Notes saves notes with Git: the package includes Git and Git Credential Manager (GitHub Desktop's build of Git for Windows), so it needs no other software, and the app doesn't link to or recommend any.

## Screenshots

PNG, 1366 × 768 to 3840 × 2160 pixels, landscape, up to 10, each under 50 MB. At least one. The files in store/screenshots/: 2560 × 1440 PNGs of the app's window at 1120 × 720, drawn at twice the scale, on a plain backdrop; the cascade lays four windows over each other. They're generated, never taken by hand: `gh workflow run review-captures.yml -f catalog=store` captures the scenes on CI, then `python tools/release/store-screenshots.py --captures <the fetched folder>` makes the PNGs (D-223).

Upload them in this order, each with its caption:

1. `01-note-light.png`: A quiet page for one note at a time, in plain Markdown.
2. `02-cascade.png`: Make it yours: ten themes, light and dark, and six fonts, including ones made for easier reading.
3. `03-spotlight-light.png`: Find any note in a few keystrokes.
4. `04-files-light.png`: Your notes are files in folders you choose.
5. `05-themes-light.png`: Pick a theme and see the whole page change at once.
6. `06-setup-welcome.png`: Start with your own GitHub account, or keep your notes on this computer only.
7. `07-setup-connect.png`: Sign in once with the GitHub account you already use.
8. `08-setup-create.png`: Focus Notes makes two repositories of your own: one for public notes, one for private ones.
9. `09-setup-creating.png`: Every step of the setup shows as it happens.
10. `10-setup-backup.png`: Notes back up to your own GitHub repository in the background, and you can see when.

## Privacy statement (from the privacy page)

> Focus Notes collects nothing about you, and neither does this site.
>
> - This site has no analytics, no cookies and no counters. Every page, font and picture comes from this site, and nothing is loaded from any other.
> - The app talks only to your computer and to GitHub, with your own account, to save and back up your notes. There's no Focus Notes server and no Focus Notes account.
> - Your private notes stay in your own private GitHub repository. Only sealed copies are published, and only the people you choose can open them.
> - Feedback goes through GitHub issues you write yourself, in public. Nothing is sent without you.
>
> Questions about privacy? Open an issue on GitHub (https://github.com/prabinpebam/focus-notes/issues).
